concept.name: Vesting schedule
concept.definition: A vesting schedule is the pre-committed timetable by which locked token allocations (team, investors, advisors) become transferable, typically combining a cliff (no tokens for an initial period) with linear or batched releases thereafter.
concept.intuition: It is a golden-handcuffs calendar: insiders earn their tokens over years instead of getting them on day one, aligning them with the project's survival.
concept.mechanics: Allocations are locked in smart contracts and released per the published schedule — common shapes are a 1-year cliff followed by 2-3 years of linear monthly unlocks, batch unlocks at the cliff, or hybrids (e.g. Solana combined no-cliff linear community release, a 1-year cliff batch unlock for seed/foundation/validators, and 50%-after-9-months-then-monthly for the team).
concept.failure_modes: Heavy cliff unlocks create cliff-edge supply shocks; schedules enforced only by promises (multisig rather than contract) can be renegotiated, and short vesting relative to project maturity leaves insiders liquid before the product proves itself.
concept.misconceptions: Vesting does not eliminate sell pressure, it only delays it — the overhang remains and markets price it in advance. A '4-year vest' with a 1-year cliff still releases a large lump at month 12.
concept.example: Uniswap's UNI allocated 21.266% to team and 18.044% to investors with 4-year vesting; the governance treasury itself vested 40%/30%/20%/10% across years 1-4, with control unlocked after a 30-day grace period.

citations.source: Keyrock research - From Locked to Liquidity: What 16,000+ Token Unlocks Teach Us
